run.question:
Something's broken — we're getting paged. Look at the app-265-prod-logs index
for the last 3 hours and tell me what's going on across our fleet.

report.summary: The paging signal is visible in app-265-prod-logs, and it is not fleet-wide: the index holds only 7 documents across the whole 24h window (all between 2026-11-22T08:04:33Z and 09:34:33Z), covering three clusters as written in the documents' own cluster field — production-us-east-1 (3 docs), production-ap-southeast-1 (2), production-eu-west-2 (2). All three ERROR documents are from production-us-east-1 and all point at the same external dependency: payment-service logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' (09:04:33Z), checkout-service logged 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' (08:04:33Z), and checkout-service then logged 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' (09:34:33Z). The same timestamps carry healthy INFO readings in the other two clusters (production-eu-west-2 checkout p95 218ms, payment 'Adyen-eu responding normally, p95 180ms'; production-ap-southeast-1 success rate 99.9%, 'All payment provider connections healthy'), which argues against a fleet-wide checkout or payment outage. In production-eu-west-2, the only cluster my Kubernetes access reads, all 21 otel-demo deployments report 1 ready/available and the checkout pod logged 273 lines from 09:59:16Z to 10:04:16Z with repeated 'payment went through' successes; the flagd-config ConfigMap there has every fault-injection flag (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, others) at defaultVariant 'off', so no injected payment fault is in effect in that cluster. Two important limits make this partial rather than supported: Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt (13 calls across both), so I could not read error-rate series, span errors, or the firing state of the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh alert defined in the prometheus ConfigMap, and I have no Kubernetes object access to production-us-east-1 or production-ap-southeast-1, so the state of the failing pods and of that cluster's flagd flags is unknown. The deepest cause the evidence supports is the stripe-us payment provider timing out calls from production-us-east-1's payment-service, which then surfaced as checkout failures and an open circuit breaker; why stripe-us times out is not observable in the available data, and the sparse 7-document log sample cannot establish when the condition began or whether it persists after 09:34:33Z.

claims.text: app-265-prod-logs contains 7 documents in the 2026-11-21T10:04:42Z–2026-11-22T10:04:42Z window, split by the documents' own cluster field into production-us-east-1 (3), production-ap-southeast-1 (2) and production-eu-west-2 (2); by level INFO (4) and ERROR (3); by service checkout-service (4) and payment-service (3).

All three ERROR documents carry cluster=production-us-east-1 and read exactly: checkout-service 2026-11-22T08:04:33Z 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)'; payment-service 2026-11-22T09:04:33Z 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'; checkout-service 2026-11-22T09:34:33Z 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)'.

In the same index and window, production-eu-west-2 emitted only INFO readings: checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 218ms' at 2026-11-22T08:04:33Z and payment-service 'Adyen-eu responding normally, p95 180ms' at 2026-11-22T09:34:33Z.

production-ap-southeast-1 emitted only INFO readings: checkout-service 'Healthy: success rate 99.9%' at 2026-11-22T08:04:33Z and payment-service 'All payment provider connections healthy' at 2026-11-22T09:34:33Z.

In production-eu-west-2, the only cluster my Kubernetes access reads, all 21 deployments in namespace otel-demo report readyReplicas=1, availableReplicas=1 and updatedReplicas=1, including checkout and payment, and all 32 pods cluster-wide are in phase Running.

Pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n (namespace otel-demo, production-eu-west-2) wrote 273 log lines between 2026-11-22T09:59:16Z and 2026-11-22T10:04:16Z, the newest 25 of which contain repeated '[PlaceOrder] ...' lines followed by 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' and 'order confirmation email sent' with severity info, i.e. successful payment calls in that cluster at that time.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in namespace otel-demo declares fault-injection flags paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%', variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off) and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), plus cartFailure, adFailure, productCatalogFailure and others, each with state ENABLED but defaultVariant 'off'; deployment flagd (image ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.12.8) mounts this ConfigMap as volume config-ro, so in production-eu-west-2 no payment fault flag is in effect.

The prometheus ConfigMap's alerting_rules.yml defines CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh on rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m]) over the all-status ratio > 0.5, for 2m, severity critical, label cluster=opspilot-m1 — a rule that would page on exactly the checkout errors seen in the logs, but its firing state is unverified.

Cluster events inside the window are only 2 FailedToCreateEndpoint events from endpoint-controller, for Endpoints orca (service app-95) at 2026-11-22T09:21:00Z and Endpoints signup-service (service app-162) at 2026-11-22T09:32:52Z ('endpoints ... already exists'); neither names or touches checkout or payment.

The page is consistent with CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh firing on production-us-east-1 checkout PlaceOrder errors: the three ERROR lines are checkout/payment failures in that cluster and the rule pages on checkout PlaceOrder error ratio > 50% for 2m, but Prometheus was unreachable so the actual alert state and error ratio were not read.

An injected payment fault switched on in production-us-east-1's own flagd configuration remains an open candidate for the payment-service 30s failures, since the demo's flagd flags include paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable; I could not read that cluster's objects (Kubernetes access is limited to production-eu-west-2), where the equivalent flags are all off.

Contemporaneous readings in production-eu-west-2 and production-ap-southeast-1 are healthy (p95 218ms and 180ms, success rate 99.9%, 'All payment provider connections healthy'), and in production-eu-west-2 the checkout pod kept completing payments through 10:04:16Z with all deployments 1/1 ready, so a fleet-wide checkout-service or payment-service outage is not supported by the logs.

Injected fault-injection flags in the production-eu-west-2 otel-demo flagd configuration are not the cause of this incident: paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable (and every other listed fault flag) are state ENABLED with defaultVariant 'off', and that cluster's checkout continued to log successful payments.

Have the on-call payment owner check stripe-us /v1/charges availability and latency toward production-us-east-1, and confirm whether checkout's 41% failure-rate circuit breaker toward payment-service has closed; then read the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh alert state and checkout/payment status_code error rates in Prometheus once the source is reachable again.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for the whole investigation: get_all_labels, get_label_values, get_metric_names, get_prometheus_target, list_prometheus_rules, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate series (traces_span_metrics_calls_total by status_code), no rpc_* latency/status series, no cluster label coverage check and no firing state for CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh were obtained.

Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services, traces_search and traces_search_by_tags all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so span-level error status, span durations and any parent-child call edge from checkout to payment or to the payment provider are unknown.

Kubernetes access covers only production-eu-west-2; the failing checkout-service and payment-service instances in production-us-east-1 (and production-ap-southeast-1) could not be inspected for pod phase, restart counts, last termination reason/exit code, events, application logs or flagd flag values, so the hypothesis of an injected payment flag there is untested.

app-265-prod-logs holds only 7 documents in the full 24h window, so the true failure volume, the start time of the stripe-us timeouts before 08:04:33Z and their state after 09:34:33Z are unknown; the last ERROR document is 09:34:33Z and nothing later is in the index.

A filtered log query on production-eu-west-2 pods checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n and payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d for error/timeout/circuit patterns returned no matching lines (status no_data, 237 and 158 lines read); that is a query result inside 09:04:42Z–10:04:42Z only and not proof those services never erred.
The cause of the stripe-us timeouts (provider-side outage, network path, credentials, rate limiting) is not observable in the available sources; no telemetry for stripe-us exists here.
No latency trend is asserted: the only latency readings are single INFO lines (checkout p95 218ms, payment p95 180ms) with no comparable baseline series.
The change_history integration is not configured, so no deployment or configuration change history for production-us-east-1 is available to correlate with the 08:04:33Z onset.
next_steps: Query Prometheus, when reachable, for traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} and the payment service's rpc status series, filtered to the production-us-east-1 cluster label, over 07:00Z–10:05Z, and read the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh alert state.

Read the production-us-east-1 flagd config (demo.flagd.json) and the checkout/payment pod states there, including restart counts and previous-container logs, to test the injected-payment-fault hypothesis.

Confirm with the payment provider owner whether stripe-us /v1/charges was degraded around 08:04Z–09:34Z on 2026-11-22, and review checkout's circuit-breaker thresholds and retry policy for payment-service.

content.alerting:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
